root: ^Butcher: Fresh cuts! Best meat in town — no tricks, no scraps, just honest fare. Step right up, don’t be shy — I’ve got something for every appetite.

c-0: ^Butcher: Beef, pork, lamb — all butchered this morning. Chops, roasts, sausages, and a few specialty cuts if you’re feeling adventurous.
^ Marrow bones for broth, steaks for your pan, smoked ham for a feast, and if you’re brave, I’ve got blood pudding and tongue.
^ Ever tried wild boar? Got a slab in the back, rare as hen’s teeth.
^Butcher: Prices are fair. I weigh every cut honest, and you’ll get your coin’s worth — no gristle, no waste.
^ If you’re short on coin, ask about the stew pack — trimmings and bones, perfect for a hearty meal.
c-1: ^Butcher: For flavor, nothing beats the lamb chops. Tender, juicy, and perfect with rosemary.
^ If you’re feeding a crowd, my smoked sausages never disappoint. And if you want to impress, the boar roast will have folks talking for weeks.
^Butcher: Learned the trade from my uncle. Started with sharpening knives, studying the cuts on paper and watching him... and finally the real work at the block.
^ he used to say, “A good butcher must know every beast by heart.” I reckon I do now.
c-2: ^Butcher: Word is the fishwife’s been selling river eels that aren’t quite fresh. I’d stick to my sausages if I were you.
